payload.set_intro: A student heats a metal sample, places it in water in an insulated calorimeter, and records the data shown. Assume that the metal and the water reach the same final temperature and that no heat is lost to the surroundings.

stimulus.description: A hot metal sample is placed in water in an insulated calorimeter

rows: Final temperature of metal and water (°C)

items.stem: What is the heat gained by the water, in J? (The specific heat of water is 4.18 J/(g °C).)

options.why: Uses the mass of the metal and the temperature change of the water.
Uses the temperature of the metal instead of the temperature change of the water.
Forgets the mass of the water.

items.explanation_en:
The correct answer is $6080\text{ J}$. q = mcΔT = (150 g)(4.18 J/(g °C))(9.7 °C) = 6080 J.
$4050\text{ J}$ is incorrect: Uses the mass of the metal and the temperature change of the water.
$19200\text{ J}$ is incorrect: Uses the temperature of the metal instead of the temperature change of the water.
$40.5\text{ J}$ is incorrect: Forgets the mass of the water.

items.stem: What is the specific heat of the metal, in J/(g °C)? (Assume that no heat is lost to the surroundings.)

options.why: Reports the specific heat of water.
The metal lost the same heat that the water gained, so c = 6080 J/((100 g)(67.3 °C)) = 0.904 J/(g °C).
Divides by the temperature change of the water instead of the temperature change of the metal.
Uses the final temperature instead of the temperature change of the metal.
